title.name: Pelotari!
title.subtitle: Hand pelota at the village frontón
menu.easy.note: You reach the ball more easily and miss less.
menu.normal.note: Three rivals, each tougher. Beat all three and win the txapela.
intro.1: It's fiesta time in the village. The bells ring and everyone heads down to the frontón.
intro.2: There's a hand-pelota tournament. Three rivals, one frontón, and for the champion, the txapela.
intro.3: Hit the ball against the front wall, above the metal band, and return it before it bounces twice.
howto.title: How to play
howto.a: [A] drive: strikes high and comes back deep
howto.b: [B] dejada: soft, dies near the wall
howto.aim: Push the stick to one side as you strike to send it there
howto.turn: You strike in turns: the coloured ring shows whose turn it is. The longer the rally, the faster it gets.
gl.frontis.name: Frontis
gl.frontis.text: The front wall: every shot has to strike it.
gl.chapa.name: Chapa
gl.chapa.text: A metal band at the foot of the frontis. If the ball hits it, it goes clonk! and it's a fault.
gl.botes.name: Two bounces
gl.botes.text: You must return the ball before it bounces twice on the floor.
gl.fuera.name: Out
gl.fuera.text: If the ball lands outside the court, on the right or at the back, the point goes to the other player.
gl.corta.name: Short
gl.corta.text: If the ball bounces before reaching the frontis, it's a fault.
gl.pared.name: Left wall
gl.pared.text: The frontón has a wall on the left: the ball can bounce off it and stay in play.
gl.dejada.name: Dejada
gl.dejada.text: A soft shot that barely leaves the frontis and dies close: it makes the other player run!
gl.tanto.name: Tanto
gl.tanto.text: Each point is a tanto. One-on-one matches are usually played to 22.
gl.saque.name: Serve
gl.saque.text: Whoever wins the point serves the next one.
gl.title: Pelotari word
fact.title: Did you know?
fact.fronton: Many villages in Navarre have a frontón, often beside the church or the town hall.
fact.ball: Traditionally, a hand-pelota ball has a boxwood core, wool, and a hand-stitched leather cover.
fact.hands: Pelotaris play bare-handed, protecting their hands with pads and tape.
fact.old: Pelota is thought to come from very old ball games played in Europe since the Middle Ages.
fact.fiestas: At fiesta time the pelota match is a must: half the village comes to the frontón.
fact.kids: In many villages, children learn to play pelota at the frontón from a very young age.
fact.modes: Besides by hand, it's played with a wooden bat, a curved basket or a racket: there are many kinds.
howto.txoko: [A] with ← txoko: into the corner, off both walls
howto.ancho: [A] with → wide: tight to the right-hand line
howto.globo: [A] with ↓ lob: very high and deep
howto.timing: Strike when the ring on the shadow turns gold: a perfect hit!
rival.txiki.name: Txiki
rival.txiki.about: The village kid. Unhurried, and gives nothing away.
rival.martillo.name: The Hammer
rival.martillo.about: Hits very hard and sends the ball wide.
rival.txapeldun.name: The Champion
rival.txapeldun.about: The district champion. A master of the dejada and the txoko.
txapela.title: Champion!
txapela.text: You won the fiesta tournament. Like real champions, you get the txapela.
gl.txoko.name: Txoko
gl.txoko.text: The corner where the frontis meets the left wall. A ball into the txoko comes out awkwardly and is hard to return.
gl.txapela.name: Txapela
gl.txapela.text: The Basque beret. In Basque sports, the champion is crowned with a txapela.
fact.txapela: In Basque sports, the winner of a championship is crowned with a txapela instead of given a cup.
help.play: [A] drive (← txoko · → wide · ↓ lob) · [B] dejada · strike on the gold ring
